# Vector Databases

**Definition:** Specialized databases designed to store, index, and query high-dimensional vector embeddings generated by machine learning models to enable semantic similarity search.

## How It Works
- Stores data objects (text, images) alongside their corresponding mathematical vector representations.
- Uses Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) algorithms, like HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World), to quickly retrieve vectors that are mathematically close to a query vector.
- Calculates semantic proximity using distance metrics like Cosine Similarity or Euclidean Distance.

## Why It Matters
- Forms the core storage retrieval layer for modern Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines and LLM-powered applications.

## Common Pitfalls
- Using exact k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN) search on massive datasets, resulting in unacceptably slow O(N) query latency instead of relying on ANN indexes.

## Related Terms
- [[Large Language Model (LLM)]]
- [[Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)]]

## Example
Pinecone and Milvus are dedicated vector databases, while pgvector is an extension that adds vector indexing capabilities directly to PostgreSQL.
